stem: While documenting the transaction, an adult receiving an opiate for outpatient acute pain for the first time presents an OxyContin prescription for eight days without exception documentation. What is the key issue?

choices.text: The initial outpatient opiate supply generally may not exceed seven days without a documented statutory exception.
Dispense the eight-day supply because extended-release opioids are exempt if its alternate trigger can be documented.
Use the ordinary 30-day Schedule II opioid quantity limit without further inquiry.
Use the 90-day non-opioid Schedule II pathway.
Split the prescription into seven days now and one day as a refill.

related_facts: oxycodone (OxyContin) is used for severe and persistent pain requiring extended opioid treatment; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.

An initial outpatient opiate prescription for an adult and any opiate prescription for a minor is generally limited to seven days, subject to documented statutory exceptions; opioid-dependence treatment is excluded.
